sentences.speaker: A
sentences.en_text: You seem a little down today. Is everything okay?
sentences.ko_word_order: 너 좀 처져 보여 / 오늘. / 다 괜찮아?
sentences.ko_natural: 오늘 좀 기운 없어 보이네. 무슨 일 있어?

terms.nuance: 슬프거나 기운이 없을 때 쓰는 구어. feel down, look down처럼 쓴다.

examples.en: I've been feeling down since Monday.
Rainy days always get me down.
He looked a bit down after the game.
examples.ko: 경기 끝나고 걔 좀 풀 죽어 보였어.

terms.nuance: 상대 상태를 조심스럽게 짐작해 말할 때 쓴다. look보다 분위기까지 포함한 느낌.

examples.en: She seems really happy these days.
You seem tired. Did you sleep okay?
That seems like a good idea.

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.en_text: Honestly, I've been really stressed out lately.
sentences.ko_word_order: 솔직히, / 나 정말 스트레스 받아 왔어 / 요즘
sentences.ko_natural: 솔직히 요즘 스트레스를 너무 많이 받아.

terms.nuance: stressed보다 지치고 압박받는 느낌이 더 강한 구어.

examples.en: Exams always make me stressed out.
Don't get stressed out over small things.
She's stressed out about her wedding.
examples.ko: 걔 결혼식 때문에 스트레스 받고 있어.

terms.nuance: 최근 한동안 이어진 일에 쓴다. 보통 현재완료(have been)와 함께 온다.

examples.en: Have you seen any good movies lately?
examples.ko: 요즘 좋은 영화 본 거 있어?

examples.en: I've been sleeping badly lately.
He's been really quiet lately.

terms.nuance: 속마음을 털어놓을 때 문장 앞에 붙인다. To be honest와 비슷하다.

examples.en: Honestly, I didn't like the food.
I honestly don't know what to do.
Honestly, you look great in that.

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.en_text: I'm sorry to hear that. What's been going on?
sentences.ko_word_order: 그 말 들으니 안타깝다. / 무슨 일이 있었어?

terms.nuance: 안 좋은 소식에 공감하며 하는 말. 사과가 아니라 위로의 sorry다.

examples.en: You lost your job? I'm sorry to hear that.
I'm sorry to hear that your dog is sick.
Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Is she okay?

terms.nuance: What's going on?은 '무슨 일이야?'. What's been going on?은 '요즘 무슨 일 있었어?'.

examples.en: What's going on out there?
Something is going on with him.
Can you tell me what's going on?

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.en_text: Work has been crazy, and I can't sleep well.
sentences.ko_word_order: 일이 정신없었어, / 그리고 나는 잘 수가 없어 / 잘
sentences.ko_natural: 회사가 너무 정신없고, 잠도 잘 못 자.

terms.nuance: 바쁘거나 혼란스러운 상황을 과장해 말하는 구어. 사람에게 쓰면 '미친'이 되니 주의.

examples.en: Traffic was crazy this morning.
It's been a crazy week.
The store is crazy on weekends.

terms.nuance: 잠을 푹 잤는지 말할 때 쓴다. 못 잤으면 I didn't sleep well.

examples.en: Did you sleep well last night?
I never sleep well in hotels.
Sleep well, and see you tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.en_text: That sounds exhausting. No wonder you look tired.
sentences.ko_word_order: 그거 진 빠지겠다. / 당연하네 / 네가 피곤해 보이는 게

terms.nuance: 몹시 지치게 만드는 일이나 상황에 쓴다. 사람이 지쳤으면 exhausted.

examples.en: Moving is so exhausting.
Taking care of twins is exhausting.
The trip was fun but exhausting.

terms.nuance: 이유를 듣고 '그래서 그랬구나' 하고 납득할 때 쓴다.

examples.en: You skipped lunch? No wonder you're hungry.
No wonder it's so cold. The window is open.
He trains every day. No wonder he's so fast.

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.en_text: Yeah, I feel like I'm always behind on everything.
sentences.ko_word_order: 응, 나는 느껴져 / 내가 항상 밀려 있는 것처럼 / 모든 일에
sentences.ko_natural: 응, 맨날 모든 일이 밀려 있는 느낌이야.

terms.nuance: 확실하지 않은 느낌이나 기분을 말할 때. feel like 뒤에 문장을 붙여 많이 쓴다.

examples.en: I feel like I've met him before.
examples.ko: 그 사람 전에 만난 적 있는 것 같아.

examples.en: I feel like nobody listens to me.
examples.ko: 아무도 내 말을 안 듣는 것 같아.

examples.en: Do you ever feel like time goes too fast?
examples.ko: 시간이 너무 빨리 간다고 느낄 때 있어?

terms.nuance: 해야 할 일이 예정보다 늦어져 쌓였을 때 쓴다.

examples.en: I'm behind on my homework.
We're two weeks behind on the project.
He got behind on his rent.

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.en_text: Have you tried talking to your boss about it?
sentences.ko_word_order: 너 해 봤어 / 상사한테 말하는 걸 / 그것에 대해?

terms.nuance: 방법을 제안하거나 물어볼 때 쓴다. try to do는 '~하려고 애쓰다'로 뜻이 다르다.

examples.en: Have you tried turning it off and on?
Try drinking some warm tea.
I tried calling her, but she was busy.

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.en_text: Not yet. I'm afraid she'll think I can't handle it.
sentences.ko_word_order: 아직. / 나는 걱정돼 / 그녀가 생각할까 봐 / 내가 감당 못 한다고
sentences.ko_natural: 아직. 내가 감당 못 한다고 생각할까 봐 걱정돼.

terms.nuance: 안 좋은 일이 생길까 걱정될 때 쓴다. 무서움보다 걱정에 가깝다.

examples.en: I'm afraid I'll be late again.
I'm afraid she won't like my gift.
examples.ko: 걔가 내 선물 안 좋아할까 봐 걱정돼.

examples.en: I'm afraid we'll miss the train.

terms.nuance: 어려운 일이나 상황을 해내다. deal with와 비슷하다.

examples.en: Don't worry, I can handle it.
examples.ko: 걱정 마, 내가 처리할 수 있어.

examples.en: He can't handle spicy food.
How do you handle so much stress?

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.en_text: I get that, but you'll feel better if you're honest.
sentences.ko_word_order: 이해해, / 하지만 너는 나아질 거야 / 만약 네가 솔직하면
sentences.ko_natural: 무슨 마음인지 알아. 근데 솔직하게 말하면 마음이 편해질 거야.

terms.nuance: 상대 입장을 이해한다는 공감 표현. I understand보다 구어적이다.

examples.en: You're nervous? I get that.
I get that you're busy, but please reply.
examples.ko: 바쁜 건 알겠는데 답장 좀 해.

examples.en: I totally get that.

terms.nuance: 몸이나 기분이 좋아질 때. 아픈 사람에게 Feel better!라고도 한다.

examples.en: Take a nap. You'll feel better.
Do you feel better today?
Talking to you always makes me feel better.

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.en_text: You're right. Thanks, I already feel a bit lighter.
sentences.ko_word_order: 네 말이 맞아. / 고마워, / 벌써 좀 가벼워졌어
sentences.ko_natural: 맞아. 고마워, 벌써 좀 마음이 가벼워졌어.

terms.nuance: 걱정을 털어놓은 뒤 홀가분해진 느낌. 몸이 가볍다는 뜻으로도 쓴다.

examples.en: After crying, I felt lighter.
Telling the truth made me feel lighter.
I feel lighter after cleaning my room.
